entities.summary: Tristán de Luna y Arellano was a Spanish conquistador who played a pivotal role in the exploration and colonization of the New World. Born in 1510 in Borobia, Spain, he was part of the elite group of explorers who accompanied Hernán Cortés on his expedition to Mexico in 1519. This journey marked the beginning of Spanish dominance in the region, with de Luna y Arellano serving as a key figure in the conquest of the Aztec Empire. De Luna y Arellano's actions had a lasting impact on the indigenous populations, leading to the destruction of their civilizations and the introduction of European diseases that decimated their numbers. The legacy of de Luna y Arellano can be seen in the many cities and landmarks that bear his name, a testament to the enduring influence of his conquests. As the Spanish Empire expanded, de Luna y Arellano's exploits were celebrated as heroic deeds, cementing his place in the annals of history as a symbol of Spanish power and ambition.
